full_judgment:
"10(2). In case of honest concurrent user of other special circumstances which, in the opinion of the Registrar, make it proper so to do he may permit the registration by more than one proprietor of trade marks which are identical or nearly resemble each other in respect of the same goods or description of goods, subject to such conditions and limitations, if any, as the Registrar may think fit to impose." 

 28. In this regard, this Court has taken note, for example, of the judgment in BCIC vs. Sattar Match Works reported in 44 DLR (AD) 1992, 208 where it was held that honest and concurrent user under Section 10(2) necessarily presupposes a satisfaction by the Registrar, and subject to conditions and limitation that he may seek to impose in that regard, as to the beneficial aspects of such possible registration of identical or similar trade marks as would protect not only the interests of competing proprietors but would also, and more importantly, secure the interest of the public in general, thereby, protecting them from possible deception and confusion.
